chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Barqī, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“The inscription on my father’s ring was: ‘All might belongs to Allah,’ and it was on his left hand, with which he would perform istinjāʾ. And the inscription on the ring of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was: ‘The dominion belongs to Allah,’ and it was on his left hand, with which he would perform istinjāʾ.”

So this report is to be understood as taqiyyah, because its narrator is Wahb ibn Wahb, and he is a non-Imami whose solitary reports are abandoned in practice, especially since what we presented earlier pertains to the etiquettes of taharah and not to its obligations.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under certain circumstances
key_terms.نَقْشُ: the engraved inscription on a ring
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: he performs istinjāʾ, cleansing after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars understand this hadith about wearing a ring on the left hand during istinjāʾ?
ai.summary: This passage cites a report about the inscriptions on the rings of the Imams عليهم السلام and their wearing them on the left hand. The author then clarifies that the report is carried on taqiyyah due to the condition of its narrator and notes that the matter relates to the etiquettes of taharah rather than its obligatory rulings.
